Goal: make packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js accept several files (and - for stdin), and open one pull request that meets every acceptance line of issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104.

What to read first: packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js (the CLI today handles one file), packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js (lint(text)), packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js (existing node:test tests that spawn the bin), packages/jsonl-lint/README.md, and .github/workflows/test.yml (the CI runs `npm ci` and `npm test` at the root on Node 22).

Steps:
1. Do not touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js. The diff must leave that file byte-for-byte the same. All new behaviour goes in packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js.
2. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js so it takes `<file> [<file> ...]` from process.argv.slice(2):
   - No arguments: print a usage line to stderr (for example `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`) and exit 2, with nothing on stdout.
   - More than one `-` argument: this is a usage error. Print a message to stderr and exit 2 before checking anything, with nothing on stdout.
   - Go through the files in the order given. For `-`, read all of stdin (readFileSync(0, 'utf8') works) and report it under the name `-`. For any other name, readFileSync(name, 'utf8'). If a file can't be read, print `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` to stderr, remember that it failed, and carry on with the rest of the files. Don't stop.
   - For each file that was read, run lint(text) and print `<file>:<line>: <error>` to stdout for each problem, using the argument exactly as given and replacing newlines in the error with spaces, the same as the one-file output today. Keep the output in file order.
   - Exit code: 2 if any file couldn't be read, otherwise 1 if any row in any file is bad, otherwise 0. Clean files print nothing. One file must behave exactly as before.
3. Add node:test tests to packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js, spawning the bin the way the existing tests do (use spawnSync's `input` option to feed stdin). Write each of these as its own clearly named test:
   - two clean files: exit 0 and empty stdout;
   - one bad file among several clean ones: exit 1, and stdout lists only the bad file's `<file>:<line>: ` lines;
   - stdin via `-` with clean input: exit 0 and no output;
   - stdin via `-` with bad input: exit 1, and the lines start with `-:<line>: `;
   - a missing file among good ones: exit 2, the missing file named on stderr, and the good files still checked (add a bad row to one of them so the test proves its lines still show up on stdout);
   - two `-` arguments: exit 2 and a message on stderr;
   - no arguments: exit 2 and a usage message on stderr.
   Keep every existing test passing.
4. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: document the usage `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`, explain that `-` reads stdin, is reported as `-`, and can be given only once (a second `-` is a usage error, exit 2), and say that files are checked in order. Update the exit codes section: 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named, `-` is given twice, or any file can't be read (error on stderr; the other files are still checked and reported).
5. Run `npm test` at the repository root and make sure it passes.
6. Commit, push and open one pull request on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test. The PR body must contain the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104` and a short summary of the change.
result.verifier:
Check the pull request for issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 at its head commit. Run every command from the repository root of a checkout of the PR head. Each command below runs on its own (no shell variable carries over from one command to the next). It writes its fixtures under /tmp/jv104 and recreates them each time. Report PASS or FAIL for each check, in order, with the output that backs it up.

Setup command, run first: `rm -rf /tmp/jv104 && mkdir -p /tmp/jv104 && printf '{"a":1}\n{"b":2}\n' > /tmp/jv104/c1.jsonl && printf '{"c":3}\n' > /tmp/jv104/c2.jsonl && printf '{"a":1}\n{bad}\n{"x":' > /tmp/jv104/b1.jsonl && printf '{oops}\n' > /tmp/jv104/b2.jsonl && ls /tmp/jv104`

Check 1. Expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before"
Run: `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jv104/b1.jsonl /tmp/jv104/c1.jsonl /tmp/jv104/b2.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"` and `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jv104/b1.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"`
PASS: the multi-file run prints `/tmp/jv104/b1.jsonl:2: <error>` and `/tmp/jv104/b1.jsonl:3: <error>` lines, then a `/tmp/jv104/b2.jsonl:1: <error>` line, in that order, and nothing for c1.jsonl. The one-file run prints lines in the same `<file>:<line>: <error>` form for b1.jsonl's rows 2 and 3.
FAIL: a named file isn't checked, the files are reported out of order, a bad row is missing, or the line format differs from `<file>:<line>: <error>`.

Check 2. Expect line: "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)"
Run: `printf '{"a":1}\n{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jv104/c1.jsonl -; echo "exit=$?"` and `printf '{"a":1}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js - -; echo "exit=$?"`
PASS: the first run prints a line starting with `-:2: ` for stdin's bad row. The second run exits 2.
FAIL: stdin isn't read when `-` is given, its row is reported under some other name, or two `-` arguments give an exit status other than 2.

Check 3. Expect line: "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)"
Run each of these:
(a) `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jv104/c1.jsonl /tmp/jv104/c2.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"`
(b) `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jv104/c1.jsonl /tmp/jv104/b2.jsonl /tmp/jv104/c2.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"`
(c) `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js; echo "exit=$?"`
(d) `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jv104/c1.jsonl /tmp/jv104/nope.jsonl /tmp/jv104/c2.jsonl 2>/tmp/jv104/err.txt; echo "exit=$?"; echo '--stderr--'; cat /tmp/jv104/err.txt`
(e) `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jv104/nope.jsonl /tmp/jv104/b2.jsonl 2>/tmp/jv104/err2.txt; echo "exit=$?"; echo '--stderr--'; cat /tmp/jv104/err2.txt`
PASS: (a) exits 0; (b) exits 1; (c) exits 2 with a message on stderr; (d) exits 2 with an error on stderr; (e) has an error about nope.jsonl on stderr and still prints the `/tmp/jv104/b2.jsonl:1: ` line on stdout, so the other file was still checked and reported.
FAIL: any of these exit statuses differs, an unreadable file gives no error on stderr, or the tool stops at the unreadable file without checking and reporting the files that remain.

Check 4. Expect line: "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged"
Run: `gh pr list --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --search 'https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104' --state all --json number,headRefOid,files` (or `gh pr view <number> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json files` for this PR), then `gh pr diff <number> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test -- 2>/dev/null | grep -n '^diff --git' ` to list the changed files.
PASS: the lint function in packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js is unchanged. Either the file is absent from the PR's changed files, or the diff touches nothing in lint(text).
FAIL: the PR diff changes the lint function in packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js.

Check 5. Expect line: "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage"
Run: `cd packages/jsonl-lint && node --test 2>&1 | tail -40`, then read packages/jsonl-lint/test/*.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md at the head.
PASS: the package's node:test tests include tests that run the CLI with each of these cases: two clean files; one bad file among several; stdin via `-` with clean input; stdin via `-` with bad input; a missing file among good ones; two `-` arguments; no arguments. The README documents the multi-file usage (`<file> [<file> ...]`) and `-` for stdin.
FAIL: any of those seven cases has no test, or the README doesn't document the usage with several files and `-`.

Check 6. Expect line: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run: `gh pr list --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --state open --search '104 in:body' --json number,body,headRefOid,url`, then `gh pr checks <number> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test`, then at the repository root `npm ci && npm test; echo "exit=$?"`.
PASS: exactly one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test is open for this change, and its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`; `npm test` passes at the head; the `test` workflow check is green for the head commit.
FAIL: there is no such PR or more than one, the body lacks that text, `npm test` fails, or the test workflow check at the head is failing, missing or still pending.

Advisory (not pass or fail conditions):
- Check that one file gives byte-identical output to before. To do that, compare with the base's bin run against b1.jsonl.
- If a file can't be read and another file has a bad row, the builder was told that exit 2 wins. Note the behaviour if it differs.
- See whether two `-` arguments print nothing on stdout and a clear message on stderr, and whether the no-argument usage message lists `<file> [<file> ...]`.
- See whether the tests are clearly named for each case and whether the README's exit code section mentions the second `-` case.
